rawOutput.title: Use the Product Rule Independently
rawOutput.rationale: This is a focused conceptual learning and problem-solving plan. It begins with the product rule and one complete worked example because the rule is new, then moves through guided use, independent retrieval, and mixed application. Four 15-minute sessions fit the available windows and keep one action prominent at a time. No knowledge-map topics were supplied, so the plan is bounded to the stated product-rule skill.

sessions.title: Understand the Product Rule
sessions.objective: Build a clear model of when and how the product rule works.
sessions.amountLabel: The rule, its parts, and one complete worked example
contentTargets: Recognize a product of two differentiable functions.
Use (fg)' = f'g + fg' in one worked example.
completionEvidence: Explain why differentiating each factor and multiplying the results is incorrect.
Apply the product rule to one closely matched problem with guidance.

sessions.title: Apply Each Step with Less Support
sessions.objective: Carry out the product-rule procedure while identifying each term.
contentTargets: Assign f, g, f', and g' correctly.
Substitute the four parts into the product-rule formula.
completionEvidence: Solve one polynomial product derivative with brief prompts.
Explain where each term in the resulting derivative came from.

sessions.title: Retrieve and Use the Rule Independently
sessions.objective: Recall the rule and solve without step prompts.
sessions.amountLabel: Rule retrieval and two independent derivatives
contentTargets: Recall the product rule without a displayed formula.
Differentiate products independently and simplify the results.
completionEvidence: Recall the product rule accurately from memory.
Solve two product-rule problems without procedural prompts.

sessions.title: Choose and Verify the Product Rule
sessions.objective: Decide when the rule is needed and check independent work.
sessions.amountLabel: Three mixed classifications and one independent application
contentTargets: Distinguish product-rule problems from direct power-rule problems.
Verify a derivative by checking structure and correcting errors.
completionEvidence: Classify three expressions by the differentiation rule they require.
Solve and verify one product-rule derivative independently.

activities.label: product-rule-recognition
activities.title: When a product rule applies
activities.body: Read the model and note the key clue.

essentialIdeas: Recognize a product of two differentiable functions.

activities.label: own-words-check
activities.title: Say the clue in your own words
activities.body: Answer from memory in one or two sentences.
activities.concept: Recognize a product of two differentiable functions.
activities.correctAnswer: A product-rule situation is when the derivative problem is for two differentiable functions multiplied together.
activities.feedback: A complete answer says the expression is a product of two differentiable functions, not just a sum or a single function. If needed, repair by naming the two factors.

activities.label: fix-the-miss
activities.title: Repair the product clue
activities.body: Revise your answer after checking the model.
activities.misconceptionSummary: Thinking the rule applies only when you see two separate terms instead of two multiplied functions.
activities.concept: Recognize a product of two differentiable functions.
activities.correctAnswer: The rule applies when the expression is a product of two differentiable functions, even if the product is written inside parentheses or with variables.
activities.feedback: The key is multiplication of two functions, not the presence of two terms. A good repair names the product directly and avoids treating addition as the trigger.

activities.label: second-explanation
activities.title: Explain the clue again
activities.body: Give a fresh explanation without copying the model.
activities.concept: Recognize a product of two differentiable functions.
activities.correctAnswer: When two differentiable functions are multiplied together, that derivative problem is a product-rule problem.
activities.feedback: The answer should be short, plain, and accurate. It is complete if it identifies the multiplication of two differentiable functions as the trigger.

activities.label: recognition-check
activities.title: Spot the product-rule case
activities.body: Choose the expression that is a product of two differentiable functions.
activities.concept: Recognize a product of two differentiable functions.
activities.feedback: The product rule is used when two differentiable functions are multiplied. The other choices are not a product of two functions.
